ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure lists four labeled Lewis structures: Methanol is shown as CH3-O-H, with the oxygen atom carrying lone pairs of electrons and connected with an O-H bond; Pentane is shown as a five-carbon chain containing only carbon and hydrogen; Acetone is shown as CH3-C(=O)-CH3, containing a carbonyl oxygen; Ether is shown as CH3-O-CH3, with the oxygen atom connected to two carbons and having lone pairs of electrons. Reasoning: Pentane contains only C and H and is overall nonpolar. Ether and Acetone both contain oxygen, so they are more polar than Pentane, but they do not have an O-H bond, and have larger hydrocarbon group portions. Methanol contains oxygen with lone pairs of electrons and an O-H bond, has the strongest polarity, and can form hydrogen bonds with polar solvents. According to the problem statement, when using a polar solvent, the most polar substance, which is most easily soluble in the polar solvent, will be carried the farthest, so Methanol should be selected.

raw_record.question_text: Based on the Lewis structures shown, which molecule would travel the farthest in a paper chromatography experiment using a polar solvent?

method.method_draft: First identify each molecule from the image and classify its polarity from its Lewis structure. Pentane is nonpolar because it contains only C and H. Ether and acetone contain oxygen, so they are more polar than pentane, but they have larger hydrocarbon portions and lack an O–H bond. Methanol contains an oxygen with lone pairs and an O–H bond, making it strongly polar and able to hydrogen bond. Since a polar solvent carries the most polar/most soluble compound farthest, choose Methanol.

planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question’s condition that the chromatography solvent is polar and that the answer must be one of the molecules shown.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: In chromatography with a polar solvent as the mobile phase, the molecule most attracted to or most soluble in the polar solvent will be carried the farthest. Molecules with highly polar bonds and hydrogen-bonding ability are more compatible with polar solvent than nonpolar hydrocarbons.

method.method_draft: Compare the four structures by hydrogen-bonding interaction with the polar solvent. Exclude pentane because it has no polar heteroatom. Ether and acetone each have oxygen atoms but cannot donate hydrogen bonds and include more hydrophobic carbon framework. Methanol is the smallest molecule and has an -OH group, so it can both donate and accept hydrogen bonds and has the least nonpolar carbon character. Therefore it should be most strongly carried by the polar solvent and travel farthest: Methanol.

再推理：按与极性溶剂的氢键作用比较，Pentane 没有极性杂原子，基本不能与极性溶剂形成强相互作用，应排除。Acetone 和 Ether 都含氧，可以作为氢键受体，但它们不能提供 O-H 氢来供氢键，并且有更多疏水碳骨架。Methanol 最小，且有 -OH 基团，既能供氢键又能受氢键，非极性碳部分最少，因此会最强地被极性溶剂带动，在纸色谱中移动最远。

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Polar solvents interact especially well with small molecules that can hydrogen bond. An O–H group provides both hydrogen-bond donation and acceptance, while carbonyls and ethers only accept hydrogen bonds, and hydrocarbons interact poorly with polar solvents. A larger hydrocarbon portion reduces polar-solvent affinity.
